
Create a FlowMap of this root timeline and attach it.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Default    |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| chunks     | [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[Any](`typing.Any`)\] | What is played, in order: each a Region of this timeline or of a descendant, a child timeline at any depth or a virtual timeline of this tree, given as the object or by its ID, or a :class:`~timetoalign.core.Gap`. | _required_ |
| id         | [str](`str`) \| None                                          | The FlowMap's ID, kept verbatim. When None, an ID with the prefix ``flow`` is minted (:class:`FlowMap <timetoalign.timelines.flow.FlowMap>`).                                                                         | `None`     |
| convention | [str](`str`) \| None                                          | Which flow of the flow control the FlowMap states; None for one written by hand.                                                                                                                                      | `None`     |
| canonical  | [bool](`bool`)                                                | Whether this is the timeline's canonical FlowMap.                                                                                                                                                                     | `False`    |
| name       | [str](`str`) \| None                                          | Optional display name.                                                                                                                                                                                                | `None`     |
| provenance | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[Any](`typing.Any`)\] | How the FlowMap was made: provenance entries.                                                                                                                                                                         | `()`       |
| seed       | [int](`int`) \| None                                          | The seed of the minter of the ID when *id* is None; not stored.                                                                                                                                                       | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type        | Description          |
|--------|-------------|----------------------|
|        | \'FlowMap\' | The created FlowMap. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description              |
|--------|----------------------------|--------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | As :meth:`add_flow_map`. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import ContinuousLogicalTimeline
>>> score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=24, uid="score")
>>> a = score.create_region(0, 16, id="a")
>>> b = score.create_region(16, 24, id="b")
>>> score.create_flow_map([a, a, "b"], id="repeat", name="with the repeat")
FlowMap('repeat', timeline='score', 3 chunks, name='with the repeat')
>>> score.get_flow_map("repeat").resolve(score).length
Coordinate(Fraction(40, 1), quarters)
```

### create_flow_map_from_measure_order { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_flow_map_from_measure_order }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_flow_map_from_measure_order(
    order,
    *,
    id=None,
    name=None,
    seed=None,
)
```

Write an order of measures a source states as a FlowMap of this root.

A source may state the order in which its measures are played
itself: the successors of a measure table
(:func:`~timetoalign.timelines.flow.measure_order_from_successors`),
or an expansion a renderer wrote out. Each stretch of measures
consecutive in the timeline's measure map becomes a Region (one
Region for a stretch played more than once), and the FlowMap lists
them in the order stated. The FlowMap says by its provenance that
the source states it (method ``imported``) and follows no
convention: it is no flow computed from flow control.

The stated order is compared with the default flow of the
timeline's flow control (:meth:`get_flow`). Where they differ a
warning is logged and the result says from where.

Each call writes its Regions and its FlowMap anew.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                   | Description                                                                                                                            | Default    |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| order  | [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[int](`int`)\] | The measure counts in the order played.                                                                                                | _required_ |
| id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                   | The FlowMap's ID, kept verbatim. When None, an ID with the prefix ``flow`` is minted.                                                  | `None`     |
| name   | [str](`str`) \| None                                   | Optional display name of the FlowMap.                                                                                                  | `None`     |
| seed   | [int](`int`) \| None                                   | The seed of one minter of the IDs of the Regions and, when *id* is None, the FlowMap, in that order; None mints each from its content. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                                     |
|--------|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'StatedFlow\' | The Regions and the FlowMap written, and where the default flow |
|        | \'StatedFlow\' | differs.                                                        |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)                                            | If this timeline is a child, holds no measure map or is not in quarters; the order is empty or names a count that is no measure of the measure map or whose length is unknown; the flow control cannot be played; or the given ID is already held. Nothing has changed then. |
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)                                              | If the flow :meth:`get_flow` returns holds a gap, which a flow played from flow control never does. Nothing has changed then.                                                                                                                                                |
|        | [UnknownLengthError](`timetoalign.timelines.base.UnknownLengthError`) | If the length is unknown.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core import Coordinate
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import ContinuousLogicalTimeline, MeasureMap
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.flowcontrol import Jump, JumpDestination
>>> score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=12, uid="score")
>>> _ = score.add_measure_map(MeasureMap.from_rows(
...     [{"count": 1, "time_signature": "4/4"}, {"count": 2}, {"count": 3}]))
>>> _ = score.flow_control.add(Jump(
...     Coordinate(8, "quarters"), [JumpDestination(repeat_count=1)], id="repeat"))
>>> stated = score.create_flow_map_from_measure_order([1, 2, 1, 2, 3], seed=7)
>>> [str(region.as_interval) for region in stated.regions]
['[0, 8) quarters', '[0, 12) quarters']
>>> stated.flow_map.chunks, stated.differs_at
(('region_1hvif5xc2r1fv', 'region_0g2wfq87pa7jx'), None)
>>> score.create_flow_map_from_measure_order([1, 2, 3]).differs_at
Coordinate(Fraction(8, 1), quarters)
```

### create_flow_maps_from_flow_control { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_flow_maps_from_flow_control }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_flow_maps_from_flow_control(
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
    actor=None,
    date=None,
    seed=None,
)
```

Write this timeline's atomic sections and its computed FlowMaps.

The flow control of the timeline and of its descendants of its unit
(:attr:`tree_flow_control
<timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.tree_flow_control>`) is played on
the timeline's axis with the three conventions
(:func:`~timetoalign.timelines.flow.engine.play`): a root plays its
whole tree, a child its own subtree. The atomic
sections (:func:`~timetoalign.timelines.flow.engine.atomic_sections`)
become Regions of the timeline, each named by its letter and stating
the type ``tts:AtomicSection`` with the provenance method
``inferred``. The ``default`` flow becomes a FlowMap listing those
Regions in the order played; ``single`` and ``printed`` become
FlowMaps only where their chunks differ from ``default``'s. Each
FlowMap names its ``convention`` and the provenance method
``inferred``.

A FlowMap names a root timeline. On a root, the Regions are the
root's, also where its flow control lies only in descendants. On a
child, the Regions are the child's and the FlowMaps are stored on
the root of its tree, listing the child's Regions; a FlowMap written there anew is named after the
child and its convention (``"Allegro, default"``). The computed
FlowMaps of a timeline are those of its root that list its Regions
only, so the flows of several children of one root stand side by
side, and a virtual timeline applying one to the root takes its new
length when it is written again.

Called again after the flow control changed, the call takes nothing
away and never lets a Region's ID name another stretch:

- an atomic section whose stretch is still one keeps its Region; it
  is renamed where the new sectioning gives it another letter;
- a stretch that is new gets a new Region, also one that was a
  section before and whose Region has been rejected since;
- a Region whose stretch is an atomic section no longer stays, with
  its ID, its interval and its name, and *actor*'s belief ``"false"``
  is recorded in its statement ``type: tts:AtomicSection``
  (:meth:`Region.with_belief <timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_belief>`),
  so that it is no atomic section any more
  (:attr:`Region.is_atomic_section
  <timetoalign.timelines.Region.is_atomic_section>`). What names it
  (a FlowMap written by hand, a statement, a Jump going on at it)
  keeps naming the same stretch;
- the computed FlowMaps keep their IDs, names and canonical flags
  and list the new sections; one written before for ``single`` or
  ``printed`` stays, also where its chunks have come to equal
  ``default``'s; a virtual timeline applying one takes its new
  length.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                   | Default           |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| believer | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | The actor whose beliefs decide which flow-control elements are read; None reads the elements no actor rejects.                                | `None`            |
| beliefs  | [Collection](`collections.abc.Collection`)\[[BeliefState](`timetoshare.BeliefState`)\] | The belief states read.                                                                                                                       | `DEFAULT_BELIEFS` |
| actor    | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | Who recomputes, an IRI: the actor whose belief rejects the atomic sections that are none any more. Needed only where there are such sections. | `None`            |
| date     | [str](`str`) \| [datetime](`datetime`).[date](`datetime.date`) \| None                 | The day of that belief, ``YYYY-MM-DD`` or a :class:`datetime.date`; today when None.                                                          | `None`            |
| seed     | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                   | The seed of one minter of the IDs of the Regions and FlowMaps written anew, in that order; None mints each from its content.                  | `None`            |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                      | Description                                                    |
|--------|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'ComputedFlows \| None\' | The atomic sections as they stand now (Regions kept and        |
|        | \'ComputedFlows \| None\' | written, in the order of the axis), the computed FlowMaps, and |
|        | \'ComputedFlows \| None\' | the findings of the ``default`` flow (those of ``single`` are  |
|        | \'ComputedFlows \| None\' | meth:`get_flow`'s); or None for a timeline whose tree holds no |
|        | \'ComputedFlows \| None\' | flow control, which writes nothing.                            |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)                                            | If the flow control cannot be played; an atomic section the timeline holds is none any more and no *actor* is given to reject it; or the date is invalid. Nothing has changed then. |
|        | [UnknownLengthError](`timetoalign.timelines.base.UnknownLengthError`) | If the length is unknown.                                                                                                                                                           |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core import Coordinate
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import ContinuousLogicalTimeline
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.flowcontrol import (
...     Jump, JumpDestination, JumpTarget)
>>> score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=12, uid="score")
>>> _ = score.flow_control.add(Jump(
...     Coordinate(8, "quarters"), [JumpDestination(repeat_count=1)], id="repeat"))
>>> written = score.create_flow_maps_from_flow_control(seed=7)
>>> [(section.id, section.name, str(section.as_interval))
...  for section in written.sections]
[('region_1hvif5xc2r1fv', 'A', '[0, 8) quarters'), ('region_0g2wfq87pa7jx', 'B', '[8, 12) quarters')]
>>> for flow_map in written.flow_maps:
...     print(flow_map.convention, flow_map.chunks)
default ('region_1hvif5xc2r1fv', 'region_1hvif5xc2r1fv', 'region_0g2wfq87pa7jx')
single ('region_1hvif5xc2r1fv', 'region_0g2wfq87pa7jx')
printed ('region_1hvif5xc2r1fv', 'region_0g2wfq87pa7jx')
>>> written.findings
()
```

A sign added at 4 divides the first section. Its Region stays
and is rejected; the last section keeps its Region under a new
letter:

```python
>>> _ = score.flow_control.add(JumpTarget(Coordinate(4, "quarters"), id="sign"))
>>> again = score.create_flow_maps_from_flow_control(
...     actor="https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097", date="2026-11-25", seed=8)
>>> [(section.id, section.name, str(section.as_interval))
...  for section in again.sections]
[('region_260an7vd22pgd', 'A', '[0, 4) quarters'), ('region_3bgc3pscka0re', 'B', '[4, 8) quarters'), ('region_0g2wfq87pa7jx', 'C', '[8, 12) quarters')]
>>> first = score.get_region("region_1hvif5xc2r1fv")
>>> str(first.as_interval), first.is_atomic_section
('[0, 8) quarters', False)
>>> again.flow_maps[0].id == written.flow_maps[0].id
True
```

### create_region { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_region }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_region(
    start,
    end,
    *,
    id=None,
    name=None,
    meta=None,
    seed=None,
)
```

Create a new Region and attach it to this timeline.

Under the unified verb×noun API, ``create`` constructs a new object,
attaches it, and returns it.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                        | Description                                                                                              | Default    |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| start  | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)         | Start coordinate.                                                                                        | _required_ |
| end    | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)         | End coordinate (must be >= start).                                                                       | _required_ |
| id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                        | The region's id, kept verbatim. When None, an id with the prefix ``region`` is minted (:class:`Region`). | `None`     |
| name   | [str](`str`) \| None                                        | Optional display name; names may repeat.                                                                 | `None`     |
| meta   | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | Optional metadata dictionary.                                                                            | `None`     |
| seed   | [int](`int`) \| None                                        | The seed of the minter of the id when *id* is None; not stored.                                          | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                             | Description                |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
|        | [Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`) | The created Region object. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                      |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the given id is already held in this manifest or end < start. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> tl.create_region(10.0, 30.0, name="Chorus")
>>> tl.create_region(30.0, 50.0, id="verse", meta={"repeat": 2})
```

### create_regions_by_grouping { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_regions_by_grouping }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_regions_by_grouping(
    field,
    *,
    name_format='{value}',
    seed=None,
)
```

Create regions by grouping *adjacent* events on a field value.

For each *run* of consecutive events that share the same value in the
specified field, creates a region spanning the run's coordinate extent
``[min_start, max_end)``. Only adjacent events with the same value are
grouped — non-adjacent occurrences of the same value produce separate
regions, which may share a name; their ids are minted.

This "run-length" semantics is essential for musical data where, e.g.,
the same time signature may recur after a change (4/4 → 3/4 → 4/4)
and each occurrence should be its own region.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                 | Description                                                                                                   | Default     |
|-------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| field       | [str](`str`)         | Event field name to group by.                                                                                 | _required_  |
| name_format | [str](`str`)         | Format string. Placeholders: {value}, {i} (0-based), {n} (1-based), {run} (1-based run index for this value). | `'{value}'` |
| seed        | [int](`int`) \| None | The seed of one minter of the regions' ids, minted in order of start; None mints each from its content.       | `None`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                               | Description                                         |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`)\] | List of Region objects ordered by start coordinate. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                        |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If field does not exist in events. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Time-signature regions (adjacent grouping)
>>> regions = tl.create_regions_by_grouping("timesig")
>>> [region.name for region in regions]
['4/4', '3/4', '4/4']
```

### create_regions_by_splitting { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_regions_by_splitting }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_regions_by_splitting(
    predicate,
    *,
    names=None,
    name_format='{prefix}_{n}',
    prefix='section',
    include_before_first=True,
    include_after_last=True,
    seed=None,
)
```

Create contiguous regions by splitting at events matching a predicate.

Finds events matching the predicate, uses their coordinates as split
points, creates contiguous regions between consecutive split points.

The predicate can be:
- A string: field name. Events where this field is truthy (non-null,
  non-empty, non-zero) are split points.
- A dict: keyword filters in the same style as ``EventData.filter()``.
  For example ``{"breaks": "section"}`` selects events whose ``breaks``
  field equals ``"section"``.
- A callable: receives event dict, returns True for split points.

For each matching event the split coordinate is the event's ``end``
(interval events) or ``start``/``instant`` (instant events).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                 | Type                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                                                               | Default          |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| predicate            | [str](`str`) \| [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| [Callable](`collections.abc.Callable`)\[\[[dict](`dict`)\], [bool](`bool`)\] | Field name, filter dict, or callable identifying split-point events.                                      | _required_       |
| names                | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                                                      | Explicit region names.                                                                                    | `None`           |
| name_format          | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                        | Format string. Placeholders: {prefix}, {i}, {n}.                                                          | `'{prefix}_{n}'` |
| prefix               | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                        | Prefix for auto-generated names.                                                                          | `'section'`      |
| include_before_first | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                      | Create a region from timeline origin to first split point.                                                | `True`           |
| include_after_last   | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                      | Create a region from last split point to timeline end.                                                    | `True`           |
| seed                 | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                                                                                | The seed of one minter of the regions' ids, minted in coordinate order; None mints each from its content. | `None`           |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                               | Description                                            |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`)\] | List of contiguous Region objects in coordinate order. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                     |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [UnknownLengthError](`timetoalign.timelines.base.UnknownLengthError`) | If ``include_after_last`` is set and the length is unknown, so that the last region has no end. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Split at section breaks
>>> tl.create_regions_by_splitting("breaks", prefix="movement")
```

```python
>>> # Split at specific break types
>>> tl.create_regions_by_splitting(
...     {"breaks": "section"}, prefix="movement"
... )
```

### create_regions_from_boundaries { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_regions_from_boundaries }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_regions_from_boundaries(
    boundaries,
    *,
    names=None,
    name_format='{prefix}_{n}',
    prefix='section',
    seed=None,
)
```

Create contiguous regions from boundary coordinates.

Given k+1 sorted boundary coordinates, creates k regions where
region_i spans [boundaries[i], boundaries[i+1]). The names label the
regions; their ids are minted.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                                                          | Description                                                                                             | Default          |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| boundaries  | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)\] | k+1 monotonically increasing coordinates.                                                               | _required_       |
| names       | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                | Explicit names for the k regions. Mutually exclusive with name_format/prefix.                           | `None`           |
| name_format | [str](`str`)                                                                                  | Format string. Placeholders: {prefix}, {i} (0-based), {n} (1-based).                                    | `'{prefix}_{n}'` |
| prefix      | [str](`str`)                                                                                  | Prefix for auto-generated names.                                                                        | `'section'`      |
| seed        | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                          | The seed of one minter of the regions' ids, minted in boundary order; None mints each from its content. | `None`           |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                               | Description                                 |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`)\] | List of k Region objects in boundary order. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                 |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If fewer than 2 boundaries or not monotonically increasing. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> regions = tl.create_regions_from_boundaries(
...     [0, 30, 60, 90],
...     prefix="movement",
... )
>>> [region.name for region in regions]
['movement_1', 'movement_2', 'movement_3']
```

### create_segment_line { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_segment_line }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_segment_line(
    boundaries,
    *,
    copy_events=True,
    seed=None,
)
```

Create a SegmentLine by segmenting at boundary coordinates.

Given k+1 sorted coordinates, produces a new SegmentLine with k
contiguous segments. Each segment's class matches self's class.
Each segment takes the events starting in its span, whole (it grows
to hold one running past its end), and, where this timeline holds
Boxes, the part of its area of an image (``meta["box"]``,
``meta["image"]``) over its span, as
:meth:`~timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_slice` states it, so a Box
keeps its shape and its start moves with the segment.

Does NOT modify self. Returns a new independent SegmentLine.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      | Default    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| boundaries  | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)\] | k+1 monotonically increasing coordinates.                                                                                                                                                        | _required_ |
| copy_events | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                | Copy events into their respective segments.                                                                                                                                                      | `True`     |
| seed        | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                          | The seed of one minter of every id the call mints, in the order built: the line, then each segment (:func:`~timetoalign.core.ids.minting_from`); without one, each from its content. Not stored. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type            | Description                        |
|--------|-----------------|------------------------------------|
|        | \'SegmentLine\' | A new SegmentLine with k segments. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If fewer than 2 boundaries or not monotonically increasing; if this timeline holds Boxes and its ``meta["box"]`` is no shape; or if it states no ``meta["box"]`` and a Box would move that a descendant holds, or one of its own into a segment not starting at 0. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> measures = audio_tl.create_segment_line(
...     [0.0] + measure_times.tolist() + [float(audio_tl.length)]
... )
```

### create_segment_line_by_grouping { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_segment_line_by_grouping }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_segment_line_by_grouping(

```

| field       | [str](`str`)         | Event field to group by.                                                                                                                                                                         | _required_  |
| copy_events | [bool](`bool`)       | Copy events into segments.                                                                                                                                                                       | `True`      |
| name_format | [str](`str`)         | Format string for segment names.                                                                                                                                                                 | `'{value}'` |
| seed        | [int](`int`) \| None | The seed of one minter of every id the call mints, in the order built: the line, then each segment (:func:`~timetoalign.core.ids.minting_from`); without one, each from its content. Not stored. | `None`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type            | Description        |
|--------|-----------------|--------------------|
|        | \'SegmentLine\' | A new SegmentLine. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                   |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If groups are not contiguous. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> systems = page.create_segment_line_by_grouping("spacing_run_id")
```

### derive { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.derive }

```python
timelines.Timeline.derive(
    target_unit,
    name=None,
    copy_events=False,
    *,
    uid=None,
    seed=None,
)
```

Create a derivative timeline in a different unit via C-Map conversion.

A ConversionMap implies the presence of a derived timeline in the
target unit. The derive() method makes this implicit timeline explicit.

The derived timeline:
- Has coordinates in the target unit
- Has length equal to the converted source length
- Automatically has an inverse C-Map back to the source unit
- Optionally copies and converts events from the source

This operation creates a NEW timeline, NOT a child timeline.
The source and derived timelines have different units, so per TTA
specification, they cannot be parent-child (children must share
the parent's unit). Use TimelineGroup to connect them.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Default    |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| target_unit | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`) | The unit for the derived timeline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | _required_ |
| name        | [str](`str`) \| None                                    | Optional name for the derived timeline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `None`     |
| copy_events | [bool](`bool`)                                          | If True, copy and convert events to the derived timeline.                                                                                                                                                                                               | `False`    |
| uid         | [str](`str`) \| None                                    | The derived timeline's id; minted when None.                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `None`     |
| seed        | [int](`int`) \| None                                    | The seed of one minter of every id the call mints, in the order built: the derived timeline (unless *uid* is given), the inverse C-Map, the copied events (:func:`~timetoalign.core.ids.minting_from`); without one, each from its content. Not stored. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                        |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | A new Timeline in the target unit. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If no C-Map exists for the target unit.            |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If C-Map is not invertible (needed for roundtrip). |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Create physical timeline with tempo C-Map
>>> audio = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=60.0)
>>> audio.add_conversion_map(LinearMap(2.0, 0.0,
...     source_unit=TimeUnit.seconds, target_unit=TimeUnit.quarters))
>>> # Derive a logical timeline
>>> score = audio.derive(TimeUnit.quarters, name="score")
>>> score.unit
TimeUnit.quarters
>>> score.length
Coordinate(120.0, quarters)  # 60 seconds * 2 q/s
```

### diagram { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.diagram }

```python
timelines.Timeline.diagram(
    width=70,

    show=None,

)
```

Generate ASCII diagram for this timeline.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type                                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Default   |
|---------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| width         | [int](`int`)                         | Total width of the diagram in characters.                                                                                                                                                                                 | `70`      |
| show_children | [bool](`bool`)                       | Whether to show child timelines (one per row).                                                                                                                                                                            | `True`    |

| unicode       | [bool](`bool`)                       | Use Unicode characters (True) or ASCII fallback (False).                                                                                                                                                                  | `True`    |

### export_to_csv { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.export_to_csv }

```python
timelines.Timeline.export_to_csv(
    filepath,
    at=None,
    conversion_maps=True,
    recursion_limit=None,
    include_events=True,
    include_boundaries=False,
    *,
    fields=None,
    units=True,
    sep=',',
    header=True,
    index=False,
)
```

Export timeline data to a CSV file.

This is a convenience method that generates a timestamp DataFrame and
writes it to a CSV file. For more control over the output, use
``get_timestamp_table(format="dataframe")`` and save manually.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name               | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                     | Default    |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| filepath           | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Output CSV file path.                                           | _required_ |
| at                 | [CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) \| [str](`str`) \| [KeyCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.KeyCollection`) \| None | Explicit positions or event IDs to use as the axis.             | `None`     |
| conversion_maps    | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)                                                                                                                                                               | C-Maps to include as additional fields. Defaults to True (all). | `True`     |
| recursion_limit    | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Maximum depth for child traversal.                              | `None`     |
| include_events     | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True and ``at`` is None, extract from events.                | `True`     |
| include_boundaries | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True, include timeline boundary coordinates.                 | `False`    |
| fields             | \'ColumnNaming \| Callable\[\[str, dict\], str\] \| list\[str\] \| None\'                                                                                                                                                           | How to name the DataFrame fields (see get_timestamp_table).     | `None`     |
| units              | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True (default), append units to field names.                 | `True`     |
| sep                | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Field separator. Default "," (comma).                           | `','`      |
| header             | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True (default), write field headers.                         | `True`     |
| index              | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True, write row indices. Default False.                      | `False`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description             |
|--------|--------------|-------------------------|
|        | [int](`int`) | Number of rows written. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from timetoalign.core import TimeUnit
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> timeline = Timeline(length=60, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_1")
>>> timeline.add_events(
...     [{"id": "beat:1", "instant": 0.0}, {"id": "beat:2", "instant": 55.0}]
... )
>>> out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> timeline.export_to_csv(str(out / "timestamps.csv"))
2
```

```python
>>> # Tab-separated, no header
>>> timeline.export_to_csv(str(out / "data.tsv"), sep="\t", header=False)
2
```

### from_dict { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.from_dict }

```python
timelines.Timeline.from_dict(data, *, timeline_id=None, name=None)
```

Read a timeline from a TimeToShare manifest.

Without *timeline_id* and *name*, a manifest holding one root
timeline and no group is read as a whole: its root is returned, and
the manifest's own keys are kept so that :meth:`to_dict` writes the
manifest back. An argument naming a timeline of the manifest, root
or descendant, selects it; given both, they must name the same
timeline. Only arguments naming no timeline override the root's id
and name, and only in a manifest of one root and no group; the new
id must not be held by any element of the manifest, and the
statements naming the root name it by its new id.

A timeline selected leaves the rest of the manifest behind: a value
of a statement of its tree naming a timeline or region of the rest
is dropped, with its provenance.

The class comes from the unit (each unit belongs to exactly one
class) and ``is_segment_line``. Every optional key may be left out
and reads as its default; a ``number_type`` left out is the unit's
own (``int`` for ticks, samples, frames and pixels, ``fraction`` for
quarters and whole_notes, ``float`` otherwise). A value on the
timeline's own axis is read as its number type decides, whatever its
lexical form (``2.0`` on an ``int`` axis is 2, ``[1, 8.0]`` on a
``fraction`` axis is 1/8); a ``length`` of ``null`` reads as None. A root's ``offset`` is kept
as :attr:`root_offset`. Keys the library does not know are kept on
the object read from the JSON object they were found in, and written
back.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                | Description                                                                                                            | Default    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| data        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | A TimeToShare manifest.                                                                                                | _required_ |
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) \| None                                | The id to select, or, when no timeline has it and the manifest holds one root and no group, the id the root takes.     | `None`     |
| name        | [str](`str`) \| None                                | The name to select, or, when no timeline has it and the manifest holds one root and no group, the name the root takes. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                              | Description        |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------|--------------------|
|        | [Timeline](`timetoalign.timelines.base.Timeline`) | The timeline read. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *data* is no TimeToShare manifest of version 0.2.0, is malformed, holds a value represented otherwise than its axis selects, if the selection matches no timeline or several, or if the id the root would take is already held in the manifest; the message names the problem, or the manifest's timelines. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> piece = Timeline.from_dict(
...     {
...         "timetoshare": "0.2.0",
...         "timelines": [{"id": "#piece", "unit": "quarters", "length": [32, 1]}],
...     }
... )
>>> type(piece).__name__, piece.length
('ContinuousLogicalTimeline', Coordinate(Fraction(32, 1), quarters))
```

### from_file { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.from_file }

```python
timelines.Timeline.from_file(path, **selection)
```

Read a manifest file in any serialization, as ``from_dict`` reads a manifest.

The text is read with ``timetoshare.loads``: canonical YAML, pretty
JSON, RFC 8785 JSON or any other JSON or YAML text. The object read
records the file's form, styling and serialization, as
``timetoshare.file_form`` reads them, and whether its timeline
objects hold ``events`` and ``external_references``, which
:meth:`to_file` writes back. An
:class:`~timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle` reads the tables its
manifest names beside it, where they lie there.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                    | Default    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| path        | [str](`str`) \| [PathLike](`os.PathLike`)\[[str](`str`)\] | The manifest file, UTF-8.                                                                                                                                                      | _required_ |
| **selection | [str](`str`) \| None                                      | The keyword arguments of ``from_dict`` that select one timeline or group of the manifest (``timeline_id`` and ``name`` for a timeline, ``group_id`` and ``name`` for a group). | `{}`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                  | Description      |
|--------|-----------------------|------------------|
|        | [Self](`typing.Self`) | The object read. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the text cannot be read (with the line and column of the fault), or ``from_dict`` refuses the manifest. |

### get_boundary_table { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_boundary_table }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_boundary_table(
    conversion_maps=True,
    recursion_limit=None,
)
```

Get timestamps for timeline boundaries only.

Returns a timestamp table containing only start (0) and end (length)
coordinates for this timeline and all children.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                            | Default   |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | C-Maps to include as fields (see get_timestamp_table). | `True`    |
| recursion_limit | [int](`int`) \| None                                                  | Maximum depth for child traversal.                     | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                     | Description                             |
|--------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) | PyArrow Table with boundary timestamps. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core import TimeUnit
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> parent = Timeline(length=60, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_1")
>>> child = Timeline(length=10, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_2")
>>> parent.add_child(child, offset=50)
>>> parent.get_boundary_table().column_names
['cpt_1', 'cpt_2']
```

Cells are coordinate structs, so read them through the frame lane
rather than ``to_pandas()`` — the latter hands back one dict per
cell:

```python
>>> parent.get_timestamp_table(
...     parent._collect_boundary_coordinates(),
...     include_events=False,
...     format="dataframe",
...     units=False,
... )
   cpt_1  cpt_2
0    0.0    NaN
1   50.0    0.0
2   60.0   10.0
```

### get_candidates { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_candidates }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_candidates(
    node=(),
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
)
```

Return the candidates: the entries of pairs the holder does not state.

A candidate is offered for someone to state (:meth:`add_statement`
with the same pair). With *believer* and the default *beliefs*, a
candidate the believer believes ``"false"`` is left out: it is not
offered to that actor again (:func:`timetoshare.candidates` with
``actor=``).

| Name     | Type                                                                                   | Description                                                                              | Default           |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| node     | [NodePath](`timetoalign.timelines.statements.NodePath`)                                | The value node whose candidates to return; ``()`` the holder.                            | `()`              |
| believer | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | The actor whose beliefs filter, an IRI (compact or absolute); every candidate when None. | `None`            |
| beliefs  | [Collection](`collections.abc.Collection`)\[[BeliefState](`timetoshare.BeliefState`)\] | The states kept, as for :meth:`get_provenance`.                                          | `DEFAULT_BELIEFS` |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                           |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *node* addresses no value node, or *beliefs* is not a collection of belief states. |

### get_children_at { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_children_at }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_children_at(coord)
```

Return all children that hold the given coordinate.

A child holds every position from its offset up to its end, and its
end too unless a sibling starts there: one boundary position belongs
to the sibling starting at it, while the end of a child nothing
follows stays on that child. A child of unknown length holds every
position from its offset on (up to its successor's offset in a
segment line). This is the rule the timeline's stamps and tables
follow, so a child listed here is a child the stamp at *coord*
names.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description              | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|------------|
| coord  | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | The coordinate to query. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                        |
|--------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[\'Timeline\'\] | List of child Timeline objects, ordered by offset. |
|        | [list](`list`)\[\'Timeline\'\] | Empty list if no children contain coord.           |

### get_conversion_map { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_conversion_map }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_conversion_map(target_unit)
```

Get a conversion map by target unit **or** by name/id.

When *target_unit* is a valid `TimeUnit` value (or an alias such as
``"seconds"``), the method returns the attached map targeting that
unit — and raises when several do, because picking one of two
readings of the same axis is the caller's decision, not this
method's.

When *target_unit* is a string that does **not** correspond to any
``TimeUnit`` member, the method falls back to a name-based lookup:
it searches first by ``cmap.id``, then by ``cmap.name``.  This is
useful for maps where source and target units are identical (e.g. a
``ShiftMap`` named ``"raw_quarters"`` that maps normalised quarters
back to raw partitura quarters).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                    | Description                                                                     | Default    |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| target_unit | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`) | A ``TimeUnit`` member, a unit alias string, or a conversion-map name/id string. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                             | Description                                             |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ConversionMap](`timetoalign.maps.ConversionMap`)\[[Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | A matching ``ConversionMap``, or ``None`` if not found. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                         |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If several attached maps target the requested unit. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> timeline.get_conversion_map(TimeUnit.seconds)
ScalarMap(...)
>>> timeline.get_conversion_map("raw_quarters")
ShiftMap(offset=-0.5, ...)
```

### get_event { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_event }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_event(event_id)
```

Look up a single event by its ``id`` field.

Searches this timeline's events first, then recursively searches
all children. When found in a child, coordinates are adjusted to
the root timeline's coordinate system.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type         | Description                         | Default    |
|----------|--------------|-------------------------------------|------------|
| event_id | [str](`str`) | The event identifier to search for. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                        | Description                                                 |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | A dictionary representing the event row, or ``None`` if not |
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | found anywhere in the hierarchy.                            |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign import Timeline, TimeUnit
>>> timeline = Timeline(length=4, unit=TimeUnit.quarters)
>>> timeline.add_events([{"id": "n1", "event_type": "Note", "start": 0, "end": 1}])
['n1']
>>> timeline.get_event("n1")["id"]
'n1'
>>> timeline.get_event("nonexistent") is None
True
```

### get_events { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_events }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_events(
    temporal_type=None,
    event_type=None,
    include_children=True,
    min_coord=None,
    max_coord=None,
    **field_filters,
)
```

Filter and retrieve events.

When ``include_children=True`` (the default), events from all
children are included with their coordinates adjusted to the
root timeline's coordinate system. Each of them names the
timeline holding it in the column ``source_timeline`` (a child, or
a deeper descendant), at every depth; the timeline's own events
leave it null. Segment events (internal bookkeeping) are always
excluded.

A bound written as a float is compared as a key, with the float
side of each event's ``start``: on a ``fraction`` axis
``min_coord=0.1`` keeps an event starting at ``1/10``, on an
``int`` axis ``min_coord=10.5`` leaves out an event starting at 10
and ``max_coord=10.5`` keeps it, and ``max_coord=math.inf`` keeps
every event. An exact bound (an ``int``, a ``Fraction``) is compared
exactly on an ``int`` or ``fraction`` axis, never rounded.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                             | Description                                                                                                                                 | Default   |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| temporal_type    | [Literal](`typing.Literal`)\[\'instant\', \'interval\'\] \| None | Filter by "instant" or "interval".                                                                                                          | `None`    |
| event_type       | [str](`str`) \| None                                             | Filter by event type name.                                                                                                                  | `None`    |
| include_children | [bool](`bool`)                                                   | If True (default), include events from all children with root-relative coordinates.                                                         | `True`    |
| min_coord        | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) \| None      | Minimum coordinate (inclusive). Can be a number in native units or a `Coordinate` with a different unit (converted via inverse C-Map).      | `None`    |
| max_coord        | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) \| None      | Maximum coordinate (exclusive). Same conversion rules as min_coord.                                                                         | `None`    |
| **field_filters  | [Any](`typing.Any`)                                              | Additional field equality filters. Each kwarg name is a field name, and the value is the required value (or a list of values for OR logic). | `{}`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                         | Description                                                   |
|--------|----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | A filtered EventData with all matching events, a table of its |
| own    | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | changing it changes nothing on the timeline.                  |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                  |
|--------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a bound is NaN, or cannot be resolved onto this timeline. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Filter by coordinate range
>>> events = tl.get_events(min_coord=10.0, max_coord=20.0)
```

```python
>>> # Filter with a Coordinate in a different unit
>>> from timetoalign import Coordinate, TimeUnit
>>> coord = Coordinate(5.0, TimeUnit.seconds)
>>> events = tl.get_events(min_coord=coord)
```

```python
>>> # Arbitrary field filters
>>> events = tl.get_events(pitch=60)  # Only middle C
>>> events = tl.get_events(pitch=[60, 62, 64])  # C, D, E
```

### get_events_at { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_events_at }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_events_at(coord, tolerance=0.0, include_children=True)
```

Get all events active at a specific coordinate.

Returns events from this timeline and all children that are
active (containing or at) the specified coordinate.

For instant events, an event is "at" the coordinate if its instant
is within tolerance of the query coordinate.

For interval events, an event is "active" if the coordinate falls
within [start, end).

A *coord* written as a float is compared as a key, with the float
side of the stored positions: on a ``fraction`` axis
``get_events_at(0.1)`` finds an event at ``1/10``, on an ``int``
axis ``get_events_at(11.5)`` finds an event spanning ``[11, 12)``.
An exact *coord* (an ``int``, a ``Fraction``) is compared exactly on
an ``int`` or ``fraction`` axis, never rounded. A float axis
compares floats whatever the query. Children are decided on this
axis too: their positions and boundaries are placed here by exact
offsets and compared with the query, so a position lies on the same
side of a child's boundary as in ``get_events(min_coord=,
max_coord=)``, and a boundary two adjoining children share belongs
to the one starting there.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                | Description                                       | Default    |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|------------|
| coord            | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | Coordinate to query (in this timeline's unit).    | _required_ |
| tolerance        | [float](`float`)                                    | Tolerance for instant event matching (default 0). | `0.0`      |
| include_children | [bool](`bool`)                                      | If True, include events from children.            | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                                  | Description                                                           |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [list](`list`)\[[dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]\]\] | Dict mapping timeline_id to list of events active at that coordinate. |
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [list](`list`)\[[dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]\]\] | Child events have coordinates in their local coordinate system.       |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                  |
|--------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *coord* is NaN, or cannot be resolved onto this timeline. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> events = score.get_events_at(50.0)
>>> events["score:1"]  # Events in root at coord 50
[{"id": "n1", "event_type": "Note", ...}]
>>> events["measure_5"]  # Events in measure 5
[...]
```

### get_flow { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_flow }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_flow(
    convention=FlowConvention.default,
    *,
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
)
```

Play this timeline's flow control and return the flow, writing nothing.

What is played is the flow control of the timeline and of its
descendants of its unit, on its axis (:attr:`tree_flow_control
<timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.tree_flow_control>`): a root plays
its whole tree, a child its own subtree.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type                                                                                   | Description                                                                                                    | Default                  |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| convention | [FlowConvention](`timetoalign.core.enums.FlowConvention`) \| [str](`str`)              | ``default`` (every Jump and Break acts), ``single`` (once through) or ``printed`` (the axis as it stands).     | `FlowConvention.default` |
| believer   | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | The actor whose beliefs decide which flow-control elements are read; None reads the elements no actor rejects. | `None`                   |
| beliefs    | [Collection](`collections.abc.Collection`)\[[BeliefState](`timetoshare.BeliefState`)\] | The belief states read.                                                                                        | `DEFAULT_BELIEFS`        |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                                                   |
|--------|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'PlayedFlow\' | The runs of the flow (:func:`~timetoalign.timelines.flow.engine.play`)        |
|        | \'PlayedFlow\' | placed one after the other: positions of this timeline's axis                 |
|        | \'PlayedFlow\' | and of the flow convert through it. Its ``findings`` are what                 |
|        | \'PlayedFlow\' | playing found on the way (a flow that never ends, a flow ending               |
|        | \'PlayedFlow\' | at a Break, a stretch never played, with its cause where                      |
|        | \'PlayedFlow\' | ``single`` leaves out what ``default`` plays); the ``printed``                |
|        | \'PlayedFlow\' | flow has none. A timeline whose tree holds no flow control is played from its |
|        | \'PlayedFlow\' | start to its end.                                                             |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                         |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [UnknownLengthError](`timetoalign.timelines.base.UnknownLengthError`) | If the length is unknown.                                                                                                           |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)                                            | If the convention is unknown, or the flow control cannot be played (two Jumps of the tree at one position of this axis among them). |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core import Coordinate
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import ContinuousLogicalTimeline
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.flowcontrol import Jump, JumpDestination
>>> score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=12, uid="score")
>>> _ = score.flow_control.add(
...     Jump(Coordinate(8, "quarters"), [JumpDestination(repeat_count=1)]))
>>> score.get_flow().length, score.get_flow("single").length
(Coordinate(Fraction(20, 1), quarters), Coordinate(Fraction(12, 1), quarters))
>>> score.get_flow().unfold(2)
[Coordinate(Fraction(2, 1), quarters), Coordinate(Fraction(10, 1), quarters)]
>>> score.get_flow().findings
()
```
